newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares edge down on faint Western interest.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares edge down on faint Western interest.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged down on Tuesday on scant volumes and faint buying interest from the West, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares slipped by 0.66 percent to 184.99 on $1.66 million in volume.
Traders forecast an easing market and low volumes until mid-January.
"There is little buying on the market and regional operators are selling at bid prices," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities trader at IK Prospekt.
He said there was more selling in the morning as operators tried to close their books to fit deals into a seven-day registration period.
Purneftegaz was among the shares in demand following an order from a big investor, Ippolitov said.
Purneftegaz rose to $2.28 from $2.18 at Monday's close.
Maxim Perlin, a trader from UFG, said there had been little interest in leading shares in the last few days, although price levels were good for buying.
He said there were some long-term orders for shares of regional telecommunications and oil holding companies.

Tomskenergo rose to $4.65 from $4.60 at Tuesday's close, Permenergo was up to $15.5 after $15.0 on December 14 close when it was last traded, LUKoil edged down to $10.30 from $10.40 and UES rose to $0.0827 from $0.0825.
